message.content:
**Answer** The sculpture most often cited as the quintessential icon of 19th‑century art is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (1889). --- ### Why “The Kiss”? | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Creation date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist, early modernism | | **Technique** | Bronze casting (originally a marble study) | | **Cultural impact** | • Became a symbol of Romantic love and sensuality.
• Influenced countless artists and public monuments.
• Widely reproduced in prints, postcards, and museum collections worldwide. | | **Legacy** | • One of Rodin’s most celebrated works, often compared with his later masterpiece “The Thinker.”
• Continues to be displayed in major museums (e.g., Musée Rodin, Paris; Musée d’Orsay, Paris). | --- ### Other contenders | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Why it matters | |-----------|--------|------|----------------| | **The Gates of Hell** | Rodin | 1880–1917 (unfinished) | Monumental scale, narrative depth, influence on modern sculpture. | | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Bartholdi | 1886 | National symbol, engineering marvel, global icon. | | **The Birth of Venus** | Alexandre Cabanel | 1863 | Classic subject reinterpreted in academic realism. | While each of these works is significant, “The Kiss” is uniquely emblematic of the 19th‑century shift toward expressive, emotionally charged sculpture, making it the most famous of its era.
